translationRepairs: His mother was Empress Xiaogongzhao, known for sincere filial devotion.
s0002 母誠孝昭皇后 names Empress Chengxiaozhao. Xiaogongzhao misorders the posthumous elements and drops 誠; the added gloss of sincere filial devotion is not a separate statement in the Chinese.
His mother was the Empress of Sincere Filiality and Zhao.
His mother was Empress Chengxiao Zhao.
The literal line splits 誠孝 and 昭 as unrelated epithets. 誠孝昭皇后 is the established posthumous name Chengxiao Zhao.
On wuchen in the eighth month Regional Commander Li Ying crushed the rebel Tibetans of Qu River in Anding; the Ding prince Sang'erjiashijia came to court to submit.
On wuchen in the eighth month Regional Commander Li Ying crushed the rebel Tibetans of Anding and Quxian; the Ding prince Sang'erjiashijia came to court to submit.
s0025 安定曲先叛番 names two localities, Anding and Quxian. 曲先 is not a river, so 'Qu River in Anding' is a real place-name error.
On guichou Zhang Ying, vice minister of rites at the southern capital, was also appointed grand secretary of the Huagai Hall with a seat in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
On guichou Zhang Ying, vice minister of rites at the touring court, was also appointed grand secretary of the Huagai Hall with a seat in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
s0282 行在禮部侍郎 is the rites vice-minister of the touring court. 行在 is not the southern capital.
In the ninth month, on the bingchen day,
In the ninth month, on the bingshen day,
s0051 丙申 is the stem-branch bingshen. Bingchen would be 丙辰.
The literal date repeats the same 丙申/bingchen error; bingshen is the correct reading.

On jisi the emperor marched in person against Gaoxu, leaving the princes of Zheng and Xiang as regents; Yangwu Marquis Xue Lu and Qingping Marquis Wu Cheng commanded the van, and the armies of the Five Chief Commissions received lavish gifts.

On jisi the emperor marched in person against Gaoxu, leaving the princes of Zheng and Xiang as regents; Yangwu Marquis Xue Lu and Qingping Earl Wu Cheng commanded the van, and the armies of the Five Chief Commissions received lavish gifts.
s0045 清平伯吳成 is an earl (伯). Only 陽武侯薛祿 is a marquis; calling Wu Cheng a marquis upgrades his rank.
On guihai in the second month Chen Shan, acting revenue vice minister at the southern capital, was promoted minister and grand secretary of the Jinshen Hall with a seat in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
On guihai in the second month Chen Shan, acting revenue vice minister of the mobile court, was promoted minister and grand secretary of the Jinshen Hall with a seat in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
s0063 行在戶部待郎 marks the mobile/touring administration. The southern capital is not in the Chinese.
On jiazi the Prince of Jin Zhu Jihuai was guilty and demoted to commoner.
On jiazi the Prince of Jin Zhu Jihuang was guilty and demoted to commoner.
s0067 晉王濟熿 is Jihuang. Jihuai misreads 熿.
In the third month on xinmao palace graduates Ma Yu and others were granted jinshi with honors, and xiucai entrants were ranked.
In the third month on xinmao Ma Yu and others were granted jinshi with honors, with the remaining ranks differentiated.
The chapter’s 出身秀差 is a graphic corruption of the standard jinshi formula 出身有差, not a ranking of xiucai. Wikisource reads 賜馬愉等進士及第、出身有差, and the replacement follows that wording.
In the third year, on jiawu in the first month, the emperor again performed the southern suburban sacrifice.
In the third year, on jiawu in the first month, the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice.
s0090 大祀天地於南郊 has no 再 or other marker of repetition. Idiomatic 'again' is invented.
On renshen summer tax was forgiven in the disaster districts of Beiping.
On renshen summer tax was forgiven in the disaster districts of Beijing.
s0106 writes 北京, the Xuande-era northern capital. Beiping is the wrong English toponym for this reign.
In the eighth month, on xinmao, the traveling secretariats at Beiping and the traveling Rear Military Commission were abolished.
In the eighth month, on xinmao, the traveling secretariats at Beijing and the traveling Rear Military Commission were abolished.
s0110 罷北京行部 likewise names Beijing, not Beiping.
On wuzi Minister of Works Huang Fu and Chen Xuan, Marquis of Pingjiang, were ordered to oversee the Grand Canal grain route.
On wuzi Minister of Works Huang Fu and Chen Xuan, Earl of Pingjiang, were ordered to oversee the Grand Canal grain route.
s0127 平江伯陳瑄 is an earl (伯), not a marquis (侯).
On the day wuzi, Minister of Works Huang Fu and the Marquis of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, were put in charge of planning the grain transport.
On the day wuzi, Minister of Works Huang Fu and the Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Xuan, were put in charge of planning the grain transport.
The literal title repeats the same 平江伯/marquis error; Earl of Pingjiang is the correct rank.

In the ninth month, on the day bingwu, six men including Censor Yu Qian and Chief Steward Zhou Chen were promoted to vice minister and sent as grand coordinators of the two capitals, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Huguang.

In the ninth month, on the day bingwu, six men including Censor Yu Qian and Chief Clerk Zhou Chen were promoted to vice minister and sent as grand coordinators of the two capitals, Shandong, Shanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, Zhejiang, and Huguang.
s0164 長史周忱 is the administrator/chief clerk of an establishment, not a household steward. Chief Clerk restores the office.

In winter, the eleventh month, on xinyou, Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Chen Xuan, Earl of Pingjiang, Vice Minister Zhao Xin, and others were summoned to reach the capital by year's end and debate the merits of grain levies.

In winter, the eleventh month, on xinyou, Chen Xuan, Earl of Pingjiang and supervisor of grain transport, Vice Minister Zhao Xin, and others were summoned to reach the capital by year's end and debate the merits of grain levies.
s0208 督漕平江伯陳瑄 names Chen Xuan as supervisor of grain transport. Grand Coordinator (巡撫) is not in the Chinese.

In winter, the eleventh month, on the day xinyou, Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Chen Xuan, the Pingjiang Earl, Vice Minister Zhao Xin, and others were summoned to reach the capital by year's end to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of grain levies.

In winter, the eleventh month, on the day xinyou, Chen Xuan, the Pingjiang Earl who supervised grain transport, Vice Minister Zhao Xin, and others were summoned to reach the capital by year's end to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of grain levies.
The literal line likewise maps 督漕 onto Grand Coordinator. Grain-transport supervision is the office named.
In the fifth month, on the day dingsi, Regional Commander Grand Coordinator Xiao Shou pacified the Wuluo tribes of Guizhou.
In the fifth month, on the day dingsi, Regional Commander and Commander-in-chief Xiao Shou pacified the Wuluo tribes of Guizhou.
s0220 總兵官都督蕭授 is Regional Commander and Commander-in-chief. 都督 is not Grand Coordinator.
In the third month, on wuyin, Shan Yun campaigned against the rebellious tribes of Ping Sien.
In the third month, on wuyin, Shan Yun campaigned against and pacified the rebellious tribes of Si'en.
The chapter’s 討症思恩 is a corrupt graph. Wikisource reads 山雲討平思恩叛蠻: 討平 is the verb 'campaign and pacify', and 思恩 is Si'en, not a place named Ping Sien.
In the third month, on the day wuyin, Shan Yun campaigned against rebellious tribes of Ping Sien.
In the third month, on the day wuyin, Shan Yun campaigned and pacified the rebellious tribes of Si'en.
The literal English repeats the false toponym Ping Sien. Wikisource’s 討平思恩 supports 'campaigned and pacified the rebellious tribes of Si'en'.
In the ninth month, on guimao, the Emperor led a frontier tour in person.
In the ninth month, on guiwei, the Emperor led a frontier tour in person.
s0246 九月癸未 is guiwei. Guimao would be 癸卯.
In the ninth month, on the day guimao, the Emperor personally led a frontier tour.
In the ninth month, on the day guiwei, the Emperor personally led a frontier tour.
The literal date repeats the same 癸未/guimao error; guiwei is required.
In the twelfth month, on jiazi, the Emperor fell ill; the Prince of Wei, Zhu Zhanshan, acted as regent to offer sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In the twelfth month, on jiazi, the Emperor fell ill; the Prince of Wei, Zhu Zhanshan, substituted to offer the sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
s0258 衛王瞻埏攝享太廟 is substitution in the ancestral-temple offering, not a political regency.
In the twelfth month, on the day jiazi, the Emperor fell ill; Prince of Wei Zhu Zhanshan acted as regent to offer sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In the twelfth month, on the day jiazi, the Emperor fell ill; Prince of Wei Zhu Zhanshan substituted in offering sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
The literal 攝享 likewise means substituting in the rite, not acting as regent.
He stood in peril yet was restored to safety—the great-grandson heir had much to do with it.
He stood in peril yet was restored to safety—the imperial grandson-heir had much to do with it.
s0267 太孫 is the imperial grandson-heir (Xuanzong relative to Chengzu), not a great-grandson.
He stood in peril yet was restored to safety—the great-grandson heir had much to do with it.
He stood in peril yet was restored to safety—the imperial grandson-heir had much to do with it.
The literal line repeats the same 太孫/great-grandson error; imperial grandson-heir is the correct kinship term.
